newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Scant progress in EU-sponsored Israeli-PLO talks.
newsitem.headline: Scant progress in EU-sponsored Israeli-PLO talks.

text.p: Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy held talks with top PLO negotiator Nabil Shaath on Sunday as part of a European bid to advance stalled Israeli-PLO peace moves ahead of a Brussels meeting of EU foreign ministers.
"(The meeting was) a real serious and sincere effort to break the impasse," Shaath told reporters after two hours of talks in a Jerusalem hotel.

But negotiators were unable to announce a hoped-for meeting between Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Levy at the 15-member European Union's General Affairs Council meeting in Brussels on Tuesday.
Shaath, who left for Europe after the talks, said Arafat had not yet decided if he would attend the Brussels meeting.
"If he (Arafat) comes there, I will be happy for there to be a meeting," Levy said.

European officials said they did not want a Levy-Arafat meeting to be superficial and hoped the sides could agree on confidence building measures, mainly to provide aid to the ailing Palestinian economy, ahead of the Brussels meeting.
Peace negotiations between Israel and the Palestinians have been at a standstill since March when Israel broke ground on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

Levy said he repeated to Shaath a demand the Palestinian Authority investigate allegations that a senior Palestinian security official sent three police officers, now in Israeli custody, to attack Jews in the West Bank.
"We want actions, not statements," Levy told reporters. "This is not a routine incident...it is their obligation to fight terrorism and violence."
Miguel Moratinos, Europe's Middle East peace envoy who arranged Sunday's meeting, said progress was made on security issues, but did not elaborate.

Arafat said on Sunday a PLO investigative committee was looking into the incident. Palestinian security forces said they had arrested several of their own police officers to question them on allegations they were involved in planning attacks.
"We are dealing with the matter very seriously. The evidence so far does not really show any conclusive link of these people to anybody else," Shaath told reporters.
"I hope that this or any other matter should not be used as a pretext to stop our efforts to break the impasse," he said.
In PLO ruled Ramallah, Jordan's Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali met Arafat to review ways of breaking the impasse in Israeli-Palestinian peace talks.
"We support the president and the Palestinian people and we will use all means available to us to support the Palestinians. If we are asked to help, we will always be there." Majali said.
On Saturday, senior Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat said the United States was formulating an initiative to end the deadlock in peace talks with Israel.
Erekat told Reuters by telephone from the United States that U.S. officials were preparing a "package deal" but would not reveal details to the sides until it had been worked out fully.
But Arafat told reporters on Sunday there were no new American initiatives.
A PLO official said an Israeli proposal presented in Washington last week, based on a decades-old initiative known as the Allon plan, could serve as the starting point for fresh talks.
Netanyahu outlined to his cabinet last month a final settlement blueprint, likened to the Allon plan, under which Israel would keep key areas of the occupied West Bank.

He has also suggested moving immediately to accelerated talks on the final status of the West Bank and Gaza Strip. Palestinians charge the proposal is a ploy to avoid carrying out existing peace deals, including further West Bank pullbacks.
